access.description:
JWT access token for authenticated requests.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

refresh.description:

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access
token expires, extending the user's session.

expired_at.description:

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:
Refresh token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new discussion board article.

This schema defines the structure for creating new articles on the discussion board. It includes essential fields required for article creation, referencing the corresponding Prisma schema for database consistency.

1. Basic Information:
   - title: Article title (required)
   - content: Article content (required)

2. References:
   - category_id: ID of the category this article belongs to (required)
   - parent_id?: ID of parent article if this is a reply (optional)

3. Additional Metadata:
   - tags?: Array of tags for categorization
   - attachments?: Array of file attachments

Example:
{
  "title": "New Discussion Topic",
  "content": "Detailed discussion content here",
  "category_id": "general",
  "parent_id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
  "tags": ["discussion", "new topic"],
  "attachments": [
    {
      "filename": "image.png",
      "filesize": 1024,
      "mimetype": "image/png",
      "url": "https://example.com/image.png"
    }
  ]
}.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching and paginating articles.

This schema defines the structure for article search requests, including pagination parameters and search criteria. It allows clients to filter articles based on various conditions such as search query, date range, author, and category.

1. Pagination Parameters:
   - limit: Number of items per page (default: 20)
   - page: Page number for pagination (default: 1)

2. Search Criteria:
   - search_query: Text search across article title and content
   - date_range?: Filter by creation date range (ISO 8601 format)
   - author_id?: Filter by author's ID
   - category_id?: Filter by category ID

Example:
{
  "limit": 10,
  "page": 2,
  "search_query": "discussion board",
  "date_range": {
    "start": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "end": "2024-12-31T23:59:59Z"
  },
  "author_id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
  "category_id": "general"
}.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.description:
Response body type representing an article attachment.

Contains detailed information about an attachment associated with an article, including its unique identifier, file name, and storage URL.

This schema is used in multiple operations: retrieving a specific attachment, creating a new attachment, and listing attachments.

The attachment entity is stored in the ArticleAttachment table in the database.

Each attachment is uniquely identified by its id, has a name representing the file name, and a url pointing to the stored file location.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the attachment.

Automatically generated using UUID v4 when the attachment is created.

This field is required and must be present in all responses.

name.description:
Name of the attachment file.

Represents the original file name when the attachment was uploaded.

This field is required and must be present in all responses.

url.description:
URL pointing to the stored attachment file.

The URL is pre-signed and points to the actual file storage location.

This field is required and must be present in all responses.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.ICreat.description:
Request body type for creating a new article attachment.

Contains the necessary information to create an attachment associated with an article.
The attachment is represented by a URL pointing to the stored file.

name.description:
Name of the attachment file.

This should be the original file name provided by the user.

url.description:
URL pointing to the stored attachment file.

This URL should be pre-signed or otherwise secured to allow access to the file.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a BBS category

This schema provides a concise summary of a BBS category, including essential identification and display information.

The summary includes:
- Unique identifier (id)
- Category name (name)
- Category slug (slug)

This information helps identify and display the category in a user-friendly manner.

IDiscussionBoardArticleVersion.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an article version.

This schema provides a concise summary of an article version, including its unique identifier, title, and creation timestamp.

It is used for listing or referencing article versions without including the full content.

The summary includes essential metadata about the version, making it suitable for use in version history lists or other contexts where a detailed summary is needed.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the version was created.

This is the date and time when this version of the article was saved or created.

The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format, including timezone information, to ensure precise tracking of when the version was made.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the article version.

This is a system-generated UUID that identifies this specific version of the article.

The ID is used for tracking and referencing this version in the database and API operations.

title.description:
Title of the article version.

This represents the title of the article at this particular version.

The title is a human-readable string that provides a summary of the article's content at this version.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a comment.

This schema provides a concise summary of a comment, including its unique identifier, a preview of the content, and the creation timestamp.

It is used for listing or referencing comments without including the full content.

The summary includes essential metadata about the comment, making it suitable for use in comment lists or other contexts where a detailed summary is needed.

content_preview.description:
Preview of the comment content.

This is a truncated version of the comment text, providing a brief glimpse into the content.

The preview is useful for displaying a summary of the comment in lists or other contexts where the full content is not necessary.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the comment was created.

This is the date and time when the comment was posted or created.

The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format, including timezone information, to ensure precise tracking of when the comment was made.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the comment.

This is a system-generated UUID that identifies this specific comment.

The ID is used for tracking and referencing this comment in the database and API operations.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a BBS member

This schema represents a concise summary of a BBS member, including essential identification information and profile details.

The summary includes:
- Unique identifier (id)
- Display name (name)
- Profile picture URL (avatar_url)

This information helps identify the member in a human-readable format while omitting sensitive details.
